questionText:

questionText:
Read the following excerpt on natural resource economics and answer the questions that follow:

In 1968, biologist Garrett Hardin published his famous essay 'The Tragedy of the Commons' in the journal Science. Hardin presented a scenario of an open-access pasture shared by independent herdsmen. Each rational herdsman seeks to maximize individual economic gain. When deciding whether to add another cow to the common pasture, the herdsman receives all the direct financial benefit (+1) from selling the animal. However, the negative impact of overgrazing caused by the additional cow is shared among all the herdsmen using the pasture, so the individual herdsman suffers only a fraction of the cost (-1/n). Consequently, every herdsman is locked into a system that compels him to expand his herd without limit—in a world that is finite. Ruin is the destination toward which all men rush, each pursuing his own best interest in a society that believes in the freedom of the commons. Hardin concluded that the only solutions to avert ecological catastrophe were either private property rights (privatization) or coercive governmental regulation ('mutual coercion, mutually agreed upon'). Decades later, political scientist Elinor Ostrom challenged this rigid dichotomy, proving that communities often self-govern common pool resources (CPRs) sustainably without either state coercion or privatization.

Question: In economic taxonomy, an open-access fishery or shared pasture is classified as a 'Common Pool Resource' because it possesses:

options.text: Low rivalness and low excludability (Pure Public Good)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Zero rivalness in consumption and easy excludability
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: High rivalness in consumption (subtraction) combined with high difficulty of excluding potential users
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Common Pool Resource Economic Traits.

options.text: High rivalness and zero difficulty of exclusion (Pure Private Good)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Common Pool Resource Economic Traits):
High rivalness in consumption (subtraction) combined with high difficulty of excluding potential users

Detailed Context:
Common Pool Resources (CPRs) are subtractable/rivalrous (one person's catch leaves less for others) yet difficult to fence or exclude users from.
Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Arrange the stages of geological coalification over hundreds of millions of years under heat and pressure:
(I) Dense ancient swamp forests and giant lycophyte ferns die, accumulating in stagnant, oxygen-poor water basins
(II) Partial microbial decomposition in anaerobic mire forms spongy, high-moisture 'Peat'
(III) Burial beneath thousands of meters of sedimentary rock compresses peat into brown, soft 'Lignite'
(IV) Intense tectonic thermal maturation and overburden pressure convert lignite into hard 'Bituminous' and finally metamorphic 'Anthracite' coal
